title: Safety-Critical Scenarios Emerge from Initial Scenes

control_signal.value: A target black-box driving policy (fixed ego, adversary and traffic policies) whose closed-loop rollouts give a criticality reward; plus an ego displacement bin (near, mid, far) as a per-agent condition.

control_mechanism.value: Stage 2 post-trains only the adversary-agent branch of a latent diffusion model with RL using a hierarchical criticality reward from simulator rollouts; displacement bins enter as conditioning tokens with classifier-free guidance.

base_model.value: Conditional latent diffusion (DiT backbone) over a vectorized goal-augmented scene autoencoder, built on ScenarioDreamer, with asymmetric causal attention so the adversary agent is invisible to other agents.

datasets.value: Waymo Open Motion Dataset (64 × 64 m crops, closest 30 agents, up to 100 lane segments); rollouts in PufferDrive; 12 combinations of ego and traffic policies (IDM, PDM, PPO variants).

metrics.value: Realism: lane-graph Urban Planning metrics, agent initial-state and goal JSD, initial collision rate. Criticality: ego-fault collision rate, TTC<3s rate, ego success rate.

controllability_evidence.value: Averaged over 12 policy combinations, AdvScene-RL reaches TTC<3s rate 5.64% versus 1.26% on logged scenes, and ego-fault collision rate 0.97%, about 7× AdvScene-Base (uncond) at 0.14%.

stated_limitations.value: RL fine-tuning mainly finds failure modes of one driving policy and does not transfer to unseen policies; generalization across planners left for future work.

notes: Controllability here means steering toward criticality against a target policy, not user-specified attributes. RL fine-tuning is the primary mechanism; displacement conditioning is secondary.
